note: The parse input begins with the attacker-controlled signed token "+inf"; cursor_ points at the 'i' of the token and strncmp matches the three input bytes "inf", entering the signed-inf float-constant handling in Parser::Next().

The token-termination guard examines cursor_[4] (offset 4 from the 'i') instead of the actual next character cursor_[3]. Because the input ends right after "inf", the NUL terminator sits at cursor_[3], so cursor_[4] is one byte past the end of the initialized input; the violated safety obligation is that the examined byte must lie within the NUL-terminated input (le(cursor_[4], cursor_[3])).

IsIdentifierStart(cursor_[4])/is_digit(cursor_[4]) dereferences the byte past the NUL terminator of the "+inf" input; reading this never-initialized byte is the uninitialized read (use-of-uninitialized-value) reported by MemorySanitizer.
